subject: Regulatory addenda feasibility: GLBA & HIPAA DPA, subprocessors, and cross-border transfers
messages:
From: Chris Paulsen <cpaulsen@evergarde-insurance.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot - GLBA/HIPAA addenda feasibility and subprocessors

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, Evergarde is planning a small pilot that will send anonymized customer claims text to Redwood for inference. Before we can move forward we need to understand a few things from a legal/compliance perspective:

- Can Redwood sign a GLBA addendum for our insurance workflows and a BAA for the limited PHI elements we may need to process?
- What is your subprocessors disclosure cadence (full list vs. limited inventory)? We need to know whether any third parties will get access to unredacted data.
- For the pilot we will have a small EU subset of test records. What mechanisms do you use for EU->US transfers (SCCs, TIA, etc.)?

I attached a simple data map (evergarde_data_map_v1.xlsx) showing fields we expect to send. Could you confirm whether the proposed flow is acceptable and whether you need additional detail?

Target timeline: we want to start ingesting test data by the week of July 13th, so a quick feasibility check would be helpful.

Thanks,

Chris
Chris Paulsen
Head of IT Operations
Evergarde Insurance
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
To: Chris Paulsen <cpaulsen@evergarde-insurance.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 10:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot - GLBA/HIPAA addenda feasibility and subprocessors

Hi Chris — great to meet earlier. Appreciate the data map; I reviewed it with Neha (security/compliance) and summarized next steps below.

Short answers up front:
- BAA + GLBA addendum: feasible for a pilot, with a limited scope (test environment only) and a short-term signature. We'll share a draft DPA/BAA bundle and a GLBA addendum for your counsel to review.
- Subprocessors: we can provide a current inventory and commit to 30-day notice for changes for pilot customers. For enterprise contracts we do a more formal approval flow.
- EU->US transfers: we currently offer SCCs (standard contractual clauses) and a documented transfer impact assessment for customers in scope; for higher-risk regulated customers we can engage our privacy team for an EU->US TIA.

What we need from Evergarde to proceed:
1) Confirm which fields in the data map are considered PHI/identifiers for your classification. Mark those as PHI if applicable.
2) Confirm the EU subset size and whether the EU records include direct identifiers.
3) Point of contact for procurement/legal to receive the DPA/GLBA draft (we will send via DocuSign).

Attachments and evidence we will provide for the pilot (initial package):
- Redwood DPA v1.3 (redwood_dpa_v1.3.pdf) — draft, includes standard SCCs language option
- Current subprocessor inventory (snapshot) — will share through secure portal once we have an NDA/POC
- SOC 2 Type 2 summary and audit contact (Neha will follow up)

Proposed timeline:
- Jun 29: Redwood sends DPA + GLBA addendum draft via DocuSign
- Jul 2: Evergarde legal returns redlines/questions
- Jul 6–9: Quick sync between technical teams to confirm data flows and key rotation
- Week of Jul 13: Pilot ingestion (if agreements are signed)

If you're OK with that cadence I'll send the DocuSign link and open a Jira ticket for tracking.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Account Executive — Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference
From: Chris Paulsen <cpaulsen@evergarde-insurance.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
Cc: Dr. Sylvia Grant <s.grant@stateboard.edu>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot - GLBA/HIPAA addenda feasibility and subprocessors

Mina — this looks good, thanks. A couple of clarifying points from our side:

- PHI/identifiers: the data map flagged by my team indicates that 'claimant_name', 'ssn_last4', and 'medical_codes' are PHI/PII for our legal team. We'll mark them in the attached file and re-upload.
- EU subset: ~120 records, pseudo-anonymized but includes hashed identifiers. We can exclude direct identifiers from the EU subset if that simplifies the transfer conversation.
- Procurement POC: legal@evergarde-insurance.com (please send the DPA/GLBA draft to that address).

Two asks: can Redwood provide a short redline-friendly DPA (track changes) and confirm whether the BAA baseline includes logging/monitoring data access exceptions (we need to know whether logs could contain transient PHI)? Also, could you point me to the portal where you publish the subprocessor snapshot?

I attached our marked data map (evergarde_data_map_v1_marked.xlsx). If you can get the DocuSign out this week, that will help us accelerate.

Thanks — Chris

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.example>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Pilot - GLBA/HIPAA addenda feasibility and subprocessors

Laura/Neha — forwarding the thread with Evergarde. They confirmed PHI fields and want SCCs for EU transfers. They asked for a redline-friendly DPA and clarity on whether logs may contain transient PHI.

Proposed approach (asks for legal/security approval):
- Approve sending DPA v1.3 via DocuSign with a redline-friendly version attached (we keep the redline as a separate Word/PDF).
- For the pilot, approve a subprocessors snapshot disclosure (not the live change feed). We will provide the snapshot through the secure portal and commit to 30-day notice on changes.
- Logging: recommend we confirm that logs can contain transient identifiers only for debugging and that these are redacted/TTL'd within 7 days. Neha, can you confirm if that TTL aligns with our current log retention policy or whether we need an exception?

If approved, I'll send DocuSign to legal@evergarde-insurance.com and open JIRA-OPS-1284 to track contract and evidence delivery.

Thanks,

Mina
Account Executive — Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference
